newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-MARTINS FIRES SIX GOALS IN BRAZILIAN SPREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARTINS FIRES SIX GOALS IN BRAZILIAN SPREE.

text.p: Adailton Martins blasted six goals -- the first four in eight minutes -- as Brazil overwhelmed South Korea 10-3 in the world youth soccer championship on Sunday.
The result gave Brazil a 100 percent winning record in their three group B matches, scoring 15 goals and conceding three, and they finished top of the standings.
Brazil coach Antonio Barraso said he was happy, but added his team should have been conceded less goals.
"Our team played very well but made mistakes in the second half. The Koreans were unlucky because they missed their scoring opportunities."
Brazil's goals came from Fernandao Da Costa (19th and 41st minutes), Martins (30th, 32nd, 35th, 38th, 62nd, 68th), Vinicius Da Silva (66th), and Junior Junior (80th).
The South Koreans replied through Lee Kwan Woo, Chung Seok Keun and Lee Jung Min in the 56th, 73rd and 90th minutes.
Brazil have a second-round match against Belgium, whose coach Ariel Jacobs said he was looking forward to the game, although it would be "a very difficult honour".
"I told the players before the game that the smallest win would take us into the second round. The players are making history, so, no matter what happens from here, we can't lose," Jacobs said.
